title: Rosh Hashanah: the world's birthday
hook: the new year marks the sixth day of creation, when people were made

segments.voice: Yesterday, the shofar on Elul mornings and the selichot. Your line was thirty days to get ready. What did you write down to make right? Today, the runway ends, and the new year begins. Day six hundred forty-four.

Most new year's celebrations are about a calendar turning over. A countdown, a ball dropping, a kiss at midnight. The Jewish new year is different, and you can hear it in the prayers. Right after the shofar is blown in the additional service, the congregation says a line in Hebrew: hayom harat olam. Today the world was conceived. Or born. Today. Not a calendar flipping. A birthday. And it isn't the Jewish people's birthday. It's everyone's.

Rosh Hashanah means head of the year. Interestingly, the Torah never uses that name for it. The Torah calls it the first day of the seventh month, "a memorial proclaimed with the blast of horns, a holy convocation." The rabbis gave it its famous name. In the Talmud, two great sages argue about when the world was created. Rabbi Eliezer says in the month of Tishrei, in the autumn. Rabbi Yehoshua says Nisan, in the spring. The prayer book follows Rabbi Eliezer for this day: the new year is the world's anniversary. A midrash makes it even more precise. If creation began on the twenty-fifth of Elul, then the first of Tishrei, Rosh Hashanah, is the sixth day. The day human beings were made. The midrash then tells the whole first day of Adam's life, hour by hour: created, given the breath of life, placed in the garden, given a command, broke it, judged, and pardoned, all before sunset. And God says to him: this is a sign for your children. As you stood before Me in judgment today and went out pardoned, so will they, every year on this day. So Rosh Hashanah holds two things at once. It's the day of judgment, solemn and serious. And it's a birthday party for the whole human race. Judgment, in this telling, is something that happens to beloved creatures, on the day they were made.
screen: `HEAD OF THE YEAR.` · `TISHREI OR NISAN?` · `THE SIXTH DAY: PEOPLE ARE MADE.` · `JUDGED AND PARDONED BY SUNSET.` · then, large: `HAPPY BIRTHDAY, WORLD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: wish the world a happy birthday. Sit, and picture the whole earth. Not an idea of it: the actual oceans, a city at night, a field, a crowded train, a baby somewhere being born right now. Every one of those people shares this birthday. If you pray, you can thank God for making the world, and for making people. If not, simply say it, quietly or out loud: happy birthday, world. Let it be as silly and as serious as it is. The bell holds the time.
Rosh Hashanah. Head of the year. The Jewish new year, remembered as the birthday of the world and the day people were made.

Your line: happy birthday, world. A week of four thanks after eating, let us bless, every language, prayer shaping the day, the king in the field, thirty days to get ready. Today, treat one stranger like it's their birthday too. Day six hundred forty-four.

howItsDone: Rosh Hashanah is observed on the first two days of Tishrei with long synagogue services, the shofar, festive meals with apples and honey and round challah, and the words 'today the world was born' after the shofar in Musaf.

original.note: Hebrew: today the world was conceived, said after the shofar on Rosh Hashanah.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Jewish version of January first.
what it means: the birthday of the world and of humanity, a day of judgment for beloved creatures.
what a scholar hears: Rosh Hashanah 10b–11a's Tishrei-or-Nisan debate and Leviticus Rabbah 29:1's sixth-day Adam.

notes: Leviticus 23:24 (JPS 1917) quoted from memory; verify wording ('a memorial proclaimed with the blast of horns').
Leviticus Rabbah 29:1: creation on 25 Elul, Adam on 1 Tishrei, the twelve hours of the first day, and 'this is a sign for your children'; confirm.
Hayom harat olam: harat can mean 'conceived' or 'pregnant with'; the script says 'conceived, or born'.
